terms.grammar: noun, third declension; also plural cōnfluentēs
evidence: Liv. 1.27.4: ad cōnfluentēs collocat castra, at the confluence of the Anio with the Tiber (Lewis & Short s.v. cōnfluō)
Traupman 203: inter cōnfluentēs Tiberim et Aniōnem
terms.gloss: a confluence, the place where two rivers meet

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 295.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.

phrases.english: at the confluence of the Tiber and the Anio
